renewable.plain_thesis: We think India keeps adding renewable capacity year after year, which helps the power producers, grid companies and equipment makers behind it. Measured over the three years to July 2026 the leaders basket returned +57.8%, the growth basket +107.1% and the solar basket +75.0%, against the Nifty 50's +23.1%. Read those with care: several holdings listed only recently, so the early part of each line tracks just the names trading at the time.
renewable.description: We think India keeps adding renewable capacity year after year, which helps the power producers, grid companies and equipment makers behind it. Measured over the three years to July 2026 the leaders basket returned +57.8%, the growth basket +107.1% and the solar basket +75.0%, against the Nifty 50's +23.1%. Read those with care: several holdings listed only recently, so the early part of each line tracks just the names trading at the time.
bullets: What drives it: India's renewable-capacity build-out lifts power & equipment firms.
How to act: pick one of three baskets - the established leaders, the pure-play growth names, or the solar supply chain.
Main caveat: much of the run predates the newer listings, and every basket has fallen since its youngest holding joined.

yes.summary: If capacity keeps being added year after year, the producers, grid firms and equipment makers behind it tend to rise together.

no.summary: If the build-out slows, these names likely track the market — broad equity exposure is the steadier bet.

renewable.caveat: Several holdings listed only recently, so the early part of each line covers fewer companies than the basket holds today - and all three are down since their youngest name listed.

clean_factors.test: r_i = a + b_mkt·MKT_exMonsoon + b_rain·RURAL_f ; genuine gate b_rain>0 & |t|>=2
clean_factors.method: FWL orthogonalized market control (MKT_exMonsoon) + RURAL_f factor; HAC t
clean_factors.spurious_note: Per the naive-vs-clean test: a name is GENUINE only if it loads positively + significantly (|t|>=2) on RURAL_f AFTER the clean MKT_exMonsoon market control. Names that looked monsoon-linked under the naive (RURAL_f+NIFTY) test but lose significance under the clean control are SPURIOUS (market beta, not rural).
clean_factors.control_factor: MKT_exMonsoon (market with Auto + FMCG sectors purged)
clean_factors.mechanical_loading_note: 73 of 82 'genuine' names are RURAL_f CONSTITUENTS — their ~+1 loading on RURAL_f is MECHANICAL (circular self-loading), so they confirm the thesis basket but are NOT independent evidence. Only 9 names load on RURAL_f significantly WITHOUT being part of it (Asian Paints, Titan, Page, Jubilant, SRF…) — these are the real cross-sectional discoveries: urban-discretionary/quality names that genuinely co-move with rural demand.

monsoon.plain_thesis: A strong monsoon lifts rural demand - tractors, fertilisers, two-wheelers and FMCG. Held straight through the three years to July 2026, the quality basket returned +33.4% and the high-beta cyclicals +46.6%, against the Nifty 50's +23.1%. The catch: rainfall forecasts change late, and a market-wide fall still drags both baskets down.
monsoon.description: A strong monsoon lifts rural demand - tractors, fertilisers, two-wheelers and FMCG. Held straight through the three years to July 2026, the quality basket returned +33.4% and the high-beta cyclicals +46.6%, against the Nifty 50's +23.1%. The catch: rainfall forecasts change late, and a market-wide fall still drags both baskets down.
bullets: What drives it: a good monsoon lifts farm income and rural spending.
How to act: own the steady quality basket, or the higher-torque cyclicals.
Main caveat: forecasts shift late in the season - the signal is noisy, and both baskets fall with the wider market.

yes.summary: A good monsoon means better farm income, and the tractor, fertiliser, two-wheeler and FMCG names that sell into it tend to rise together.

no.summary: A weak monsoon squeezes rural spending — these names usually lag, so broad equity exposure is the steadier bet.

monsoon.caveat: Rainfall forecasts shift late in the season, and a market-wide fall drags these names down with it.
